messages:
maria: heads-up — dashboards popped an odd spike: invoke.validation_errors spiked ~3x at 14:03 UTC for route /v1/chat.invoke. Not sure if it's a real regression or double-counting from retries. anyone see this?

infra-bot: alert: invoke.validation_errors > 100/min for route=/v1/chat.invoke (14:03 UTC). Incident link: https://internal.redwood/alerts/7890 :rotating_light:

jay: I saw the same. The logs show a flurry of tool-call rejects with schema_mismatch, but each incoming request sometimes spawns 2 adapter retries (fallback path), so counts could be inflated.

oliver: can you paste a couple of raw log lines? curious about fields we use to dedupe in telemetry (request_id vs original_request_id)

maria: here's a truncated example from the runtime agent:```json
{"ts":"2026-02-11T14:03:12Z","route":"/v1/chat.invoke","req_id":"req_aa12","orig_req_id":"req_aa12","tool":"knowledge_search","validation":"fail","reason":"schema_mismatch","retry":0}
{"ts":"2026-02-11T14:03:12Z","route":"/v1/chat.invoke","req_id":"req_aa12_r1","orig_req_id":"req_aa12","tool":"knowledge_search","validation":"fail","reason":"schema_mismatch","retry":1}
```

oliver: aha — runtime emits a new req_id per retry (req_aa12_r1) but orig_req_id is set. Our metrics pipeline is summing by req_id, so retries appear as separate failures. we should aggregate by orig_req_id for validation fail counters.

sara: that makes sense. But note: some clients intentionally send multiple independent calls (not retries) that share no orig_req_id. we can't blindly dedupe without losing signal. we need a rule: if orig_req_id present, count once, else count per req_id. also keep retry_count tag for debugging.

jay: +1. Another nuance: quotas. Current quota dashboard counts any failed tool invocation towards route quota. Product expects only successful token usage to charge. Which behaviour do we want for validation fails? charge or not?

devex-joe: product asked last week to not charge customers for early validation rejects (they're pre-flight). But infra folks worried about exploit where clients spam validation calls to bypass quota.

maria: proposal: two-tier accounting: 1) telemetry_metric invoke_validation_attempts_total (counts every validation attempt, deduped by orig_req_id when available), 2) billing_metric tokens_consumed_total (only increments on successful model/tool output tokens). Quota enforcement should use billing_metric. The Console should surface both: attempts (for ops) and billed tokens (for customers).

oliver: implementation detail: add a tagging field validation.dedup_key = orig_req_id if present else req_id. Then in metrics pipeline: sum by (route,validation.reason,validation.dedup_key) and collapse dedup_key cardinality via cardinality reducer (count unique). For Prometheus-ish query: `count_over_time(label_replace(invoke_validation_attempts_total{route="/v1/chat.invoke"}, "dedup_key", "$1", "orig_req_id", "(.*)")[5m])` — or better done in the ingestion layer.

jay: ingestion change is safer (reduce cardinality explosions in Prom). we can add a small transform: if orig_req_id exists, emit metric with label orig=orig_req_id and drop req_id label. else emit req_id. Also emit retry_count label.

infra-bot: deploy queued: metrics-transformer v2.3 -> staging at 16:00 UTC.

sara: UX ask: Console needs a toggle to sample validation failures at 1%, 10%, 100% per route so we can capture example payloads without overwhelming storage. Current sampling is global and client-side so it's noisy. We need server-side sample and a box to "include original request body" and "include redacted PII" options.

devex-joe: agree. Also would be great to see a small "why this failed" card in the Route detail: top 3 failure reasons (schema_mismatch, missing_required, type_error) + a quick link to a sampled example. Avoid showing full customer data by default.

maria: security note: sampled payloads must go to a separate secure bucket with KMS and restricted ACLs. We already have infrastructure for crash dumps; reuse that pattern.

oliver: tech question: do we want to change the runtime HTTP header contract? e.g., accept `X-Original-Request-Id` and propagate it through all retries and adapters. That will simplify dedupe and tracing.

jay: yes. Add header `X-Original-Request-Id` required for client SDKs that implement retries. runtime will set it on first receive if absent (generate uuid) and copy to child reqs. This avoids blowing up agent logs.

maria: quick hackable curl to reproduce locally (from infra test harness):```bash
curl -X POST https://staging.redwood/api/v1/chat.invoke -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Original-Request-Id: test-req-42" -d '{"prompt":"hi","call_tool":"knowledge_search"}'
```

jay: QA plan: run 10k synthetic calls with intermittent adapter failures and verify invoke_validation_attempts_total unique count equals number of orig ids. I'll own the test.

sara: UI wire: I'll sketch a compact control: sampling dropdown + checkbox "include sample payloads" + sample retention slider. Will share Figma link by EOD.

maria: action items: @jay implement ingestion dedupe and add retry_count label (owner jay), @oliver runtime header propagation and set orig_req_id if missing (owner oliver), @sara console sampling UX and secure bucket policy (owner sara), @devex-joe update SDKs docs about X-Original-Request-Id (owner devex-joe). I'll file a tracking ticket and link PRs.

infra-bot: ticket created: PLATFORM-8732 "validation telemetry dedupe & sampling" (https://internal.redwood/PLATFORM-8732)

jay: timeline: aim for staging deploy of transformer by tomorrow morning, prod gated on results next week.

maria: thanks all. if anyone finds counterexamples where orig_req_id is ambiguous (proxies modifying headers), post here. otherwise we'll roll the transformer in staging and follow up with metrics diffs. :thumbsup:
